title: Budget and Revenue
text:
This page compares the budgets versus revenues of films in the dataset. Figure 1 shows the relationship between how much a film costs to produce and how much revenue it earns.

# import libraries
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# load dataset
films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

# make scatter plot
plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])

# adding labels
plt.xlabel("Budget (Million USD)")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (Million USD)")
plt.title("Film Budget vs. Revenue")

# display plot
plt.show()







Figure 1: Relationship between film budgets and worldwide revenues.

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
This page explores the relationship between film runtime and IMDb ratings. Figure 1 shows whether longer films tend to receive higher or lower ratings.

# import libraries
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# load dataset
films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

# make scatter plot
plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])

# add labels
plt.xlabel("Runtime (Minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb Rating")
plt.title("Film Runtime vs. IMDb Rating")

# display plot
plt.show()







Figure 1: Relationship between film runtime and IMDb ratings.

title: The Bond Films
text:
Revenue Over Time

# make line plot
